log.limits: Scope: 149 roster entries with list contiguous-48 and official_name A through L (the brief estimated about 170). Population found for 78 of 149; no published figure was found for the rest, mostly small California rancherias and several Oklahoma, Michigan, Washington and Arizona nations (for example Agua Caliente, Hopi, Colorado River Indian Tribes, Cheyenne-Arapaho has only an old state figure, Delaware Tribe of Indians, Eastern Shawnee, Kickapoo Tribe of Oklahoma, Keweenaw Bay, Lac Vieux Desert, Little River Band, Cowlitz, Jamestown S'Klallam, Lower Elwha, Chehalis, Chitimacha, Cayuga, Eastern Shoshone, Hoopa, Jicarilla). Many counts are rounded ('over', 'about') and most official pages are undated; for those, as_of is the access date (2026-11-21) and confidence is medium. Some state pages give two different figures on the same page; those are marked low. Sites refusing curl: aguacaliente.org (also failed in WebFetch), fortpecktribes.org, ctsi.nsn.us, estoo-nsn.gov, fmyn.org, koinationsonoma.com, crit-nsn.gov, lowersioux.com, bishoppaiute.net; I did not try to bypass these by imitating a browser and used WebFetch instead (facts from WebFetch say so in the note). bridgeportindiancolony.com returned 503. No directory website for Capitan Grande and Kialegee, and no official site found by search for Alturas, Big Lagoon, Cabazon, Cahto, Fort Bidwell, Grindstone, Guidiville, Inaja-Cosmit, Crow Creek, Chippewa Cree or Jackson (Jackson's directory entry is its casino site; Chippewa Cree's is the Rocky Mountain Tribal Leaders Council page; Crow Creek's is the South Dakota state page). Language tags are ISO 639-3 / BCP 47 codes chosen by me from the language the source names; where the source did not name the language exactly, the note says the tag was assigned by the researcher. Self-designations were recorded only where the nation's site (or a state page, at medium/low) states the name; Kiowa self-names on kiowatribe.org use a special font that did not survive text extraction, so none were recorded. No leader names or personal contacts were recorded; only generic office emails. The Cherokee Nation and Eastern Band pages show Cherokee syllabary, but I did not record a syllabary self-designation because I could not confirm exactly which words form the name. The North Carolina page also profiles state-recognized tribes (for example Haliwa-Saponi, Meherrin); they were out of scope and were not recorded.
log.narrative: I crawled each nation's own website (directory URL) with curl, extracted text, and searched it for enrollment counts, language names, self-designations and generic office emails, reviewing every snippet by hand before recording it. For nations without a count on their own site, I used state agency pages that publish per-nation enrollment (Montana, South Dakota, Wisconsin, North Carolina, Oregon Department of Education, Oklahoma State Department of Education) and the Inter Tribal Council of Arizona, plus a few official PDFs found by search (Kiowa annual report, Lummi community plan, Grand Traverse media kit). Bulk state pages worked well; per-nation web searches were slow and often found nothing. California rancherias rarely publish counts. Values keep the source's spelling and diacritics (for example Nʉmʉnʉʉ, Ql̓ispé, Schitsu’umsh, Kaáⁿze Íe, nsəlxcin, Weyíiletpuu).
